adjudication_note: The cited evidence contains the stated paper title and authors; the formal claim is non-propositional but textually supported.
Evidence directly states that CHT analyzes battery-pack aerodynamics/heat transfer and enables more realistic aero-thermal coupling.
Evidence supports fuel-ignition hazards from lightning/corona and battery/hybrid-power-system hazards.
Evidence directly states that cryogenic tank design/manufacture/insulation/integration are challenging because lower fuel density requires larger tanks.
Evidence directly states the need to transition from LT PEM to HT PEM to obtain a larger coolant-to-airstream temperature differential.
Evidence directly states that operation outside peak performance can cause thermal runaway unless active thermal control is provided.
The cited thermal-management passage directly supports all four listed fuel-cell thermal-management considerations.
Evidence supports frequency-domain ultrasonic defect detection and identifies the technique as a practical extension of LURS.
The cited evidence directly discusses thermoacoustic heat-pump systems; the formal claim is a topic label rather than a full proposition.
The cited evidence discusses X-57 battery temperature, runaway risk, and cooling, but not bulky containment systems or their added battery weight.
Evidence directly links defect-related geometry/material changes to ultrasonic wave propagation and wave-defect interaction, supporting detectability.
`E1` is a malformed placeholder rather than a technical proposition and is not established as a claim by the cited evidence.
Evidence directly states that active cooling can reduce battery-pack weight but adds cooling-pump weight/power that must be offset.
Evidence directly states that ultrasonic NDE can monitor internal battery parameters and potentially detect critical defects before failure.
Evidence directly states that existing safety rules can presume fossil-fuel/fire hazards while omitting battery-pack hazards of hybrid systems.
